Archive many pages in the Wayback Machine

Source: R/wayback_save.R
wbsave.Rd

Asks the Internet Archive to take a dated copy of each web page or file in a list, so that the exact source an analysis used (a statistics page, a data download, a policy document) can be cited and checked later even if the original changes or disappears. It needs a free archive.org account and its API keys.

Saves every URL in the Internet Archive's Wayback Machine with Save Page Now 2, the API archive.org offers to account holders, keeping several captures in flight at once while keeping to archive.org's rate limits. A page archived recently is kept as it is (within); a page archive.org has already captured today (its daily limit) is recorded with that capture. Each result is written to output as it arrives, so an interrupted run started again with the same output carries on where it stopped. A live progress bar shows the run while a person is watching.

Usage

wbsave(
  urls,
  ak = NULL,
  sk = NULL,
  within = "30d",
  jobs = 4L,
  output = NULL,
  poll = 10,
  maxwait = 600,
  capall = FALSE,
  quiet = NULL,
  permin = 6,
  maxcap = 1000
)

Arguments

urls

Character vector of http or https URLs. Duplicates, NA and empty strings are dropped. An address on your own network (a private or loopback IP, a .local or one-label name) is refused: the archive cannot reach it, and the request would tell it where your intranet is.

ak, sk

Your archive.org S3-like API keys (https://archive.org/account/s3.php). By default they are read from the environment variables IA_S3_ACCESS_KEY and IA_S3_SECRET_KEY, or from the files named by IA_S3_ACCESS_KEY_FILE and IA_S3_SECRET_KEY_FILE (a key file other users can read is warned about). They are sent to web.archive.org only and never printed.

within

Keep a capture made within this long instead of making a new one: a number followed by s, m, h or d (default "30d"); "0" always captures.

jobs

Captures in flight at once, 1 to 12. Default 4.

output

Optional path of a JSON Lines file: one line per URL, written as each finishes, and read at the start so a run can be resumed. Its folder must exist; this is checked before anything is sent.

poll

Seconds between status checks of a capture. Default 10.

maxwait

Seconds a capture may take before it is given up as failed. Default 600.

capall

Also capture error pages (4xx and 5xx); default FALSE.

quiet

TRUE for no progress output; the default shows it while a person is watching.

permin

Captures started per minute, at most; default 6 (archive.org allows an account 7).

maxcap

The most captures this run starts; default 1000. The rest are left for the next run (with the same output, it carries on from them).

Value

A data frame of class rmbl_wayback_save, one row per URL with a result: url, status ("saved", a new capture; "existing", a capture already there; "failed"; or "submitted", a capture started when the run was stopped, polled again by the next run), timestamp (YYYYMMDDhhmmss), snapshot (the archived copy's address) and message (archive.org's reason, for a failure). The attribute not_sent lists the URLs this run did not start (maxcap, or archive.org's daily cap for the account).

Details

Captures start no faster than permin. When archive.org asks the run to slow down (HTTP 429, or a reply saying the account has too many captures running, inside an HTTP 200 as SPN2 sends it), nothing more is submitted until the wait is over: as long as its Retry-After says, or 15 seconds doubling to 10 minutes; eight such replies in a row stop the run. A reply saying the account's daily cap is reached stops submitting for the day. A server error or a lost connection is retried with back-off, up to six times per URL; status checks that fail back off the same way. A refused key (HTTP 401 or 403) stops the run.

A run of many URLs is slow by design: at the default 6 captures a minute, 1,000 URLs take close to three hours. URLs already finished in output are skipped, so a run can be stopped and restarted.

Network: every request goes to https://web.archive.org; the keys travel in the Authorization header and are never written to output or printed.

Errors, all raised before anything is sent: no usable URL; a URL with an invisible or control character, or not starting with http:// or https://; missing keys, or keys that are not letters and digits; within not of the form "30d"; jobs outside 1 to 12; poll below 1; maxwait below poll; permin outside (0, 60]; maxcap below 1; capall not TRUE or FALSE; an output whose folder does not exist or that cannot be written.

References

Internet Archive. Save Page Now 2 (SPN2) public API.
https://archive.org/details/spn-2-public-api-page-docs

See also

wbsnpnat to look up an existing capture; wbrtry; arccap for URLs whose server refuses the Internet Archive ("cannot find" although the page is there); rmbl wayback FILE runs this from the command line.

Examples

# The checks run before any request, so these need no network or keys:
try(wbsave("ftp://example.org/report.pdf"))
#> Error : not an http(s) URL: ftp://example.org/report.pdf
try(wbsave("https://example.org/", ak = "abc", sk = "def",
                 jobs = 20))
#> Error : `jobs` must be a whole number from 1 to 12
try(wbsave("https://example.org/", ak = "abc", sk = "def",
                 output = file.path(tempdir(), "no-such-folder", "runs.jsonl")))
#> Error : the folder for `output` does not exist: /tmp/RtmpRWwpgK/no-such-folder

# A real run needs archive.org keys and the network.
if (FALSE) { # interactive()
Sys.setenv(IA_S3_ACCESS_KEY_FILE = "~/.config/ia/s3_access_key.txt",
           IA_S3_SECRET_KEY_FILE = "~/.config/ia/s3_secret_key.txt")
res <- wbsave(c("https://www.ontariocourts.ca/ocj/statistics/",
                      "https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/tbl/csv/35100177-eng.zip"),
                    output = "snapshots.jsonl")
res
}
